the Divine Liturgy noun

also liturgy, Divine Liturgy

modern

M-O s.v. Anglican: lītūrgia Anglicāna, id est certus modus ōrātiōnis (Tursellinus, 1652)

1Lītūrgia: long i and u (not in Lewis & Short; Neo-Latin texts write it without marks). Greek λειτουργία: ει and ου are long, and Latin writes them ī and ū, as in Nīlus (Νεῖλος) and Mūsa (Μοῦσα).

Dīvīna Lītūrgia1, Dīvīnae Lītūrgiae f.

The Eucharistic service of the Orthodox churches and of the Eastern Catholics; in the Byzantine rite, the Liturgies of St John Chrysostom and St Basil. In the Latin rite the same service is the Mass (missa). Lītūrgia is the Greek λειτουργία, a public service; in Neo-Latin it also means a church’s whole order of worship (Morgan–Owens).

Other words

  • synaxis, synaxis f. — the gathering for the Eucharist

    noun, third declension · also used · late Latin · Ven. Fort. Carm. 8.17 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. service: mass

    Greek σύναξις, a gathering (Lewis & Short); sacra synaxis, the Eucharistic assembly (Morgan–Owens).

See also Mass, communion, church, priest.

SourcesLewis & Short: synaxis

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. Anglican; service: mass.

Lītūrgia is not in Lewis & Short, Traupman or Levi–Bini.
